translationRepairs: Fu said: "Are there people who are as fond of beauty and as handsome as Chen Ping yet remain poor and lowly forever?"
Fu said: "Has there ever been a man as handsome as Chen Ping who remained poor and lowly forever?"

好美如陳平 names Chen Ping's fine looks; the original's 'fond of beauty and as handsome' is a double reading the Chinese does not support. The rhetorical 人固有…者乎 is correctly recast as 'has there ever been'.
In the end he gave him his daughter.
In the end he gave him his granddaughter.
Preceding 女孫 and following 誡其孫 show 卒與女 continues the granddaughter marriage, not a gift of Zhang Fu's own daughter.
At this time Wan Shi Jun Fen was the Han King's attendant and received Ping's visit, bringing him in to see Ping.
At this time Lord Wanshi Fen was the Han King's personal attendant; he received Ping's visiting card and ushered Ping in.
受平謁 is receipt of Ping's visiting card; 入見平 is Ping being ushered in. The original's 'bringing him in to see Ping' is self-contradictory and unfaithful.
The Han King said: "Young man, set it aside."
The Han King summoned Ping and rebuked him, saying: "Sir, you served Wei without success, then served Chu and left; now you follow me—should a trustworthy man have so many hearts?"

The original English is unrelated to the Chinese. 召讓平 introduces a rebuke that 先生 served Wei without success, left Chu, and now follows Han, questioning whether a trustworthy man should have many hearts.
As for performing merit and granting fiefs and cities, he is generous with them, but scholars also do not attach themselves for this reason.
As for rewarding merit with ranks and fiefs, he is reluctant to do so, and scholars therefore do not attach themselves to him.

重之 in this contrast with Han's later 饒人以爵邑 means Xiang Yu is reluctant/stingy in granting ranks and fiefs, so the original 'generous' is inverted. The proposed parenthetical gloss is awkward; the revised wording keeps the correction in natural literal English.
Look at Chu—there are those who can be caused to rebel. Xiang Yu's backbone ministers like Prime Minister, Zhongli Mei, Long Ju, Zhou Yin and such are only a few people.
Look at Chu—there are those who can be thrown into disorder. The King of Xiang's backbone ministers, men such as Yafu, Zhongli Mei, Long Ju, and Zhou Yin, number no more than a handful.
亞父 is Fan Zeng's honorific Yafu, not an office 'Prime Minister'. 可亂者 is a vulnerability to disorder, not that people can be caused to rebel.
Seeing the Chu envoys, he pretended to be astonished and said: "I thought it was the Prime Minister's envoy, but it is Xiang Yu's envoy!"
Seeing the Chu envoys, he pretended to be astonished and said: "I thought it was Yafu's envoy, but it is the King of Xiang's envoy!"
亞父使 is Yafu's envoy and 項王使 the King of Xiang's envoy; glossing 亞父 as Prime Minister and 項王 as Xiang Yu misnames both.
Xiang Yu indeed greatly doubted the Prime Minister.
Xiang Yu indeed greatly doubted Yafu.
The object of 大疑 is 亞父 (Yafu), not a prime minister.
The Prime Minister wished to urgently attack and conquer Xingyang city, but Xiang Yu did not believe him and refused to listen.
Yafu wished to urgently attack and conquer Xingyang city, but Xiang Yu did not believe him and refused to listen.
The subject who urges the assault on Xingyang is 亞父 (Yafu), not a prime minister.
The Prime Minister heard Xiang Yu doubted him, then angrily said: "The realm's affairs are greatly settled, let the king handle them himself!
Yafu heard Xiang Yu doubted him, then angrily said: "The realm's affairs are greatly settled, let the king handle them himself!
The speaker who hears the king's suspicion and angrily resigns the affair is 亞父 (Yafu), not a prime minister.
Yet troops are trapped between Jing and Suo, grain exhausted under Xingyang, cannot go west beyond Xingyang, this is Chu's critical danger.
He had not yet reached Pengcheng on the way home when a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.
The original English is an unrelated siege line. The Chinese records that on the way home, before reaching Pengcheng, a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.
Chen Ping said: "Has anyone known of Xin's rebellion?"
Chen Ping said: "The person who submitted a letter saying Xin is rebelling—has anyone else known of it?"
The question is whether anyone knows of the memorial accusing Xin of rebellion (人之上書言信反), not whether the rebellion itself is public knowledge.
Said: "The generals and officers who practice war, how do they compare to Chu's?"
Ping said: "Among Your Majesty's generals who use troops, is there anyone who can surpass Han Xin?"
The original English belongs to another comparison with Chu. This unit asks whether any of the emperor's generals who use troops can surpass Han Xin.
Said: "Using troops, who can surpass Han Xin?"
Ping said: "Now the troops are not as elite as Chu's, and the generals cannot match him, yet to raise troops and attack him is to rush him into battle—I privately fear for Your Majesty."
The original restates the previous question. This unit warns that Han troops are less elite than Chu's and the generals cannot match Xin, so a direct attack would rush into battle.
Chen Ping said: "Now troops do not equal Chu's excellence, generals cannot match, yet sending troops to attack him is inviting battle—privately I fear for Your Majesty.
Ping said: "In ancient times the Son of Heaven made inspection tours and assembled the feudal lords."
The original English is the prior warning. This unit begins Ping's plan from ancient 天子巡狩，會諸侯.
In the south there is Yunmeng. Your Majesty need only pretend to tour Yunmeng and assemble the feudal lords at Chen."
The original attributes Gaozu's 'what to do' question to this unit. The Chinese is Ping's Yunmeng ruse: pretend to tour Yunmeng and assemble the lords at Chen.
Ping said: "Anciently, the Son of Heaven toured and met with the feudal lords. Mingtang was where the people gathered.
Chen lies on the western border of Chu. When Xin hears that the Son of Heaven is touring for pleasure, he will surely think nothing is amiss and come out to the suburbs to welcome him."
The original invents Mingtang and restates the tour. The Chinese identifies Chen as Chu's western border and predicts that Xin will come out to the suburbs to welcome a pleasure tour.
Now Your Majesty wishes to meet the feudal lords at Chen. Now Chu King also claims to be emperor, with Your Majesty meeting Chen, there would be no place for Your Majesty."
When he comes to pay respects, Your Majesty can seize him—this is only the work of a single strong man."
The original invents a Chu king's claim to emperorship. The Chinese is the seizure plan: when Xin pays respects, seize him—the work of one strong man.
Emperor Gaozu approved, sent envoys telling the feudal lords to assemble at Chen, announcing, "I will tour Yunmeng in the south."
The original is a stray question. Gaozu approves, sends envoys to assemble the lords at Chen, and announces a southern tour of Yunmeng.
Ping said: "Anciently the Son of Heaven toured, met with feudal lords."
上因隨以行 means the emperor thereupon set out; 隨 is sequential, not accompaniment. The original misattributes Ping's antiquarian remark, but 'set out with them' invents traveling companions.
Southern has Yunmeng, Your Majesty falsely tours Yunmeng, meets feudal lords at Chen.
Before they reached Chen, King Xin of Chu indeed came out to welcome him along the road.
The original repeats earlier counsel. The Chinese reports that before they reached Chen, King Xin of Chu indeed came out to welcome him on the road.
Chen is Chu's western border, trustworthy hears the Son of Heaven with good intentions tours, his intentions must be without affairs, will surely come out to welcome and receive.
Gaozu had warriors ready in advance; when he saw Xin arrive he had him seized, bound, and loaded on a rear carriage.
The original misreads 信 as 'trustworthy' and restates the plan. Gaozu had warriors ready, seized and bound Xin on arrival, and loaded him on a rear carriage.
Welcomes and receives, then Your Majesty can seize him—this is only one strongman's affair."
Xin cried out: "The realm is already at peace; I of course should be boiled alive!"
The original is still the seizure plan. Xin cries out that with the realm at peace he of course should be boiled.
Gaozu thought it good, sent envoys to command the feudal lords to meet at Chen, "I will tour Yunmeng in the south.
Gaozu turned and said to Xin: "Do not make a sound!"
The original belongs to the earlier Yunmeng summons. Gaozu turns to Xin and tells him not to make a sound.
The emperor went along with it."
The original narrates departure. This unit continues Gaozu's speech: Xin's rebellion is already plain.
Went not to Chen, Chu King Xin truly welcomed along the road.
The warriors bound his arms behind his back.
The original restates the welcome on the road. 武士反接之 is the warriors binding Xin's arms behind his back.
Gaozu prepared martial warriors beforehand, saw Xin arrive, immediately bound him, loaded on rear chariot.
He then assembled the feudal lords at Chen and completely settled the territory of Chu.
The original restates the capture. This unit is the subsequent assembly of the lords at Chen and the settling of Chu territory.
Xin called: "World already pacified, I surely should be boiled!"
Returning to Luoyang, he pardoned Xin as Marquis of Huaiyin, and divided tallies with meritorious officials to confirm fiefs.
The original is Xin's outcry. Returning to Luoyang, the emperor pardons Xin as Marquis of Huaiyin and divides tallies to confirm fiefs.
Gaozu looked back and said to Xin: "Do not speak!
He then divided a tally with Ping, hereditary without end, as Marquis of Huyou.
The original is Gaozu silencing Xin. This unit is Ping's Huyou investiture: a hereditary tally as Marquis of Huyou.
Ping declined, saying, "This was not your servant's merit."
The original is Gaozu's treason charge. Ping declines the fief, saying it was not his (the servant's) merit.
Thus, met feudal lords at Chen, completely pacified Chu territory.
Ping said: "Without Wei Wuzhi, how could your servant have been introduced?"
The original restates the Chen assembly. Ping credits Wei Wuzhi: without him, how could the servant have been introduced?
The next year, as Protector of the Army Commandant he followed in attacking the rebel King Han Xin of Dai.
The next year, as Commandant Protector of the Army he followed in attacking the rebel King Han Xin of Han in Dai.
韓王信於代 is King Xin of Han (韓) campaigning/rebelling at Dai; Dai is the theater, not his royal title. The original's 'King Han Xin of Dai' misnames him.
Gaozu returned from breaking Bu's army, wounded by illness, slowly proceeded to Chang'an.
Gaozu returned from breaking Bu's army, ill from his wounds, and slowly proceeded to Chang'an.
病創 is illness from battle wounds, not being 'wounded by illness' as a separate sickness.

Using Chen Ping's plan, he summoned the Marquis of Jiang Zhou Bo to receive the command under the bed, saying: "Chen Ping quickly ride the imperial post carriage to carry Bo to replace Kuai as general. When Ping arrives at the army, immediately behead Kuai!"

Using Chen Ping's plan, he summoned the Marquis of Jiang Zhou Bo to receive the command at the bedside, saying: "Chen Ping quickly ride the imperial post carriage to carry Bo to replace Kuai as general. When Ping arrives at the army, immediately behead Kuai!"
受詔床下, with the emperor ill, is receipt of the edict at the bedside, not physically under the bed.
Zhou Bo said: "Fan Kuai because of Empress Lu has closeness;
Before they reached the army, they built an altar and summoned Fan Kuai with the tally.
The original English is unrelated dialogue. Before reaching the army they built an altar and summoned Fan Kuai with the tally (節).
Empress Lu is a woman, how can she live long?

Kuai received the edict and was at once bound behind the back, loaded into a prison cart, and relayed to Chang'an; the Marquis of Jiang, Bo, was ordered to take command and lead troops to pacify Yan's rebellious counties.

The original English is an unrelated remark about Empress Lu. Kuai is bound, loaded in a prison cart, and sent to Chang'an, while the Marquis of Jiang, Bo, takes command to pacify Yan's rebel counties.
Ping arrived at the army, beheaded him.
On the way he met a messenger with an edict ordering Ping and Guan Ying to garrison Xingyang.
The original invents Ping beheading Kuai. A messenger edict orders Ping and Guan Ying to garrison Xingyang; there is no execution here.
Ping constantly produced extraordinary strategies, always beneficial to the state, unwilling to produce dark plots.
Empress Dowager Lu was moved by his grief and said: "You have labored; go out and rest."
The original does not translate this unit. 呂太后哀之 after Ping's weeping is being moved by his grief, not merely pity; her speech tells him he has labored and should go out to rest.

Gaozu attacked Qing Bu south, Ping was ill, could not follow, Empress Lu asked: "Chen Ping follows Gaozu in campaigns, constantly resides in the center using extraordinary strategies, finally succeeds.
Ping feared that slander would take hold, so he firmly requested to remain on night-guard duty in the palace.
The original is a different Qing Bu anecdote. Ping feared slander would take hold and insisted on remaining in palace night-guard duty.
Ping said: "Zhou Bo is a blunt and strong man, can be made grand command.
Thereafter Lu Xu's slanders could not take effect.
The original is unrelated advice about Zhou Bo. Thereafter Lu Xu's slanders could not take effect.
Empress Lu asked: "Who can replace Chen Ping?"
When Fan Kuai arrived, he was pardoned and had his rank and fief restored.
The original invents Empress Lu asking who can replace Ping. When Fan Kuai arrived he was pardoned and had rank and fief restored.
Ping said: "Wang Ling can, but Ling is somewhat blunt, Chen Ping can assist him.
In the sixth year of Emperor Xiaohui, Chancellor Cao Shen died; Wang Ling, Marquis of Anguo, was made Right Chancellor, and Chen Ping Left Chancellor.
The original is invented dialogue. In Xiaohui's sixth year Chancellor Cao Shen died; Wang Ling, Marquis of Anguo, became Right Chancellor and Chen Ping Left Chancellor.
But Ping from Chu defection, Ling always treated him well.
Wang Ling was originally a man of Pei; at first he was a county strongman. When Gaozu was still obscure, he served Ling as an elder brother.
The original does not translate this unit. Wang Ling was a man of Pei and a county strongman; when Gaozu was still obscure he treated Ling as an elder brother.
But Ling's wife has wisdom, Ling cannot go against his wife's words.
Ling had little refinement, was given to temperament, and loved blunt speech.
The original invents Ling's wife. The Chinese describes Ling himself: little refinement, given to temperament, fond of blunt speech.
Empress Lu asked: "Ling's wife has wisdom, what is it?"
When Gaozu rose at Pei and entered Xianyang, Ling also gathered several thousand followers and stayed in Nanyang, refusing to follow the Lord of Pei.
The original is unrelated dialogue. When Gaozu rose at Pei and entered Xianyang, Ling gathered several thousand followers, stayed in Nanyang, and refused to follow the Lord of Pei.
Ping said: "Ling's mother is the same mother as Lu Xu, the various Lu wish to make kings, Ling's mother always says it is inappropriate.
Only when the King of Han returned to attack Xiang Ji did Ling attach his troops to Han.
The original invents shared maternity with Lu Xu. Only when the King of Han returned to attack Xiang Ji did Ling attach his troops to Han.
After Ling's mother had privately seen the envoy off, she wept and said: "For this old woman, tell Ling to serve the King of Han carefully."
The original drops the farewell. After privately seeing the envoy off, Ling's mother weeps and tells him to serve the King of Han carefully.
Asked: "Cao Shen what kind of person?"
I will see the envoy off with my death.
The original asks about Cao Shen. Ling's mother says she will see the envoy off with her death.
Ping said: "Cao Shen has wild strategy, governs the realm, comforts the people, none surpass Shen."
She then fell on a sword and died.
The original is invented Cao Shen praise. She then fell on a sword and died.
Ping said: "Cao Shen has wild strategy, governs the realm, comforts the people, none surpass Shen."
The King of Xiang was furious and boiled Ling's mother.
The original repeats the Cao Shen line. The King of Xiang, enraged, boiled Ling's mother.
Ling finally followed the King of Han and helped settle the realm.
The original asks what kind of person Chen Ping is. Ling finally followed the King of Han and helped settle the realm.
Said: "Chen Ping has surplus intelligence, but difficult to use alone."
Because he was on good terms with Yong Chi, Gaozu's enemy, and because Ling had originally had no intention of following Gaozu, he was enfeoffed late, as Marquis of Anguo.
The original omits Yong Chi and the late Anguo enfeoffment. Ling was enfeoffed late as Marquis of Anguo because he was close to Yong Chi, Gaozu's enemy, and had not meant to follow Gaozu.
After the Marquis of Anguo had been Right Chancellor for two years, Emperor Xiaohui died.
The original asks what kind of person Wang Ling is. After two years as Right Chancellor, Emperor Xiaohui died.
Said: "Wang Ling is somewhat blunt, can be made general, but cannot lead troops alone."
Empress Dowager Gao wished to make the various Lus kings. She asked Wang Ling, and Wang Ling said: "It must not be done."
The original replaces the episode with a character sketch. Empress Dowager Gao wished to make the Lü kings; Wang Ling said it must not be done.
When Ling resigned as prime minister, Empress Lu then moved Ping to be right prime minister, making Marquis of Piyang Shen Yiji left prime minister.
When Ling was dismissed as prime minister, Empress Lu then moved Ping to be right prime minister, making Marquis of Piyang Shen Yiji left prime minister.
陵之免丞相 is removal from the chancellorship (免), not a voluntary 'resignation' as the original has it; the following transfers follow that dismissal.

Lu Xu often slandered before, saying Chen Ping had advised Gaozu to execute Fan Kuai, frequently slandered saying: "Chen Ping as prime minister does not handle affairs, daily drinks strong wine, plays with women."

Lu Xu, because Chen Ping had formerly advised Gaozu to seize Fan Kuai, repeatedly slandered him, saying: "Chen Ping as prime minister does not handle affairs, daily drinks strong wine, and sports with women."
謀執樊噲 is a plan to seize/arrest Fan Kuai, not to execute him. 常以前…數讒 marks repeated slander from that earlier grudge.
主臣 is a stock exclamation of alarm and humility before the throne, not the words 'Master servant'.
Year 2 died, son Marquis Jian Hou Ji inherited the marquisate.
In the second year he died, and his son Hui, Marquis Jian, inherited the marquisate.
The heir's given name is 恢 (Hui), not Ji; 簡侯 is the marquis title Marquis Jian, which the original garbles as 'Marquis Jian Hou Ji'.
Year 23 He committed the crime of raping his subordinate's wife, beheaded, fief abolished.
In the twenty-third year He was convicted of abducting another man's wife, executed in the marketplace, and the fief was abolished.
略人妻 is abducting another person's wife, not raping a subordinate's wife; 棄市 is marketplace execution, not specifically beheading.
When he was cutting meat on the butcher's block, his ambitions were already far-reaching.
When he was cutting meat on the sacrificial board, his ambitions were already far-reaching.
俎 here is the sacrificial cutting board of the village-altar meat division, not a commercial butcher's block.
